System.Management.Automation.purpose: The engine assembly itself hosts the commands that implement engine features: command discovery and help (`Get-Command`, `Get-Help`, `Update-Help`, `Save-Help`), modules (`Import-Module`, `Get-Module`, `New-Module`, `New-ModuleManifest`, `Export-ModuleMember`), jobs (`Start-Job`, `Get-Job`, `Receive-Job`, ...), remoting (`Invoke-Command`, `*-PSSession`, `*-PSSessionConfiguration`, `Enable/Disable-PSRemoting`), the pipeline-shaping commands `ForEach-Object` and `Where-Object`, host-output commands (`Out-Default`, `Out-Host`, `Out-Null`, `Format-Default`), history, `Set-StrictMode`, `Set-PSDebug`, `Register-ArgumentCompleter` and experimental-feature commands, plus the six built-in providers (Alias, Environment, FileSystem, Function, Registry (Windows), Variable). Because they live in the engine assembly, these commands can use engine internals directly.
System.Management.Automation.responsibilities: Engine-integrated commands; unlike the other families, they are not loaded through a module manifest but through built-in registration tables.
System.Management.Automation.extension: Providers are declared with `[CmdletProvider(name, capabilities)]`; the built-in set is registered in `InitialSessionState.cs`. See [provider-model](../03-runtime/provider-model.md).
System.Management.Automation.security: Several commands are policy-relevant surface rather than ordinary cmdlets: `Invoke-Command`/`*-PSSession`/`*-PSSessionConfiguration` (remoting and JEA configuration), `Import-Module`/`New-ModuleManifest`/`Test-ModuleManifest` (module load trust), `Set-PSDebug`, `Enter-PSHostProcess`. Their enforcement points are catalogued in Phase 5 (`UNVERIFIED` until then).
System.Management.Automation.decisions: Putting `ForEach-Object` and `Where-Object` in the engine assembly (rather than the Utility module) keeps the two most-used pipeline commands available in every host and gives them privileged access to the pipeline machinery (`INFERENCE` from their location; `FACT-SRC` for the location).
System.Management.Automation.enterprise: The engine-hosted set cannot be trimmed without editing the engine; the registration tables are static. A new shell should make the built-in set data-driven.

lessons.text: Register built-in commands from a declarative table (name -> implementing type -> help) as PowerShell does, but generate the table from attributes at build time so it cannot drift from the classes.
Keep `ForEach-Object`/`Where-Object` as engine-level commands with direct pipeline access so script-block pipelines do not pay module-load or binding overhead.

System.Management.Automation.open: - `UNVERIFIED`: the exact initial-session-state table boundaries for providers, aliases and variables (only cmdlet entries were extracted).

Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Utility.purpose: General-purpose utility commands: object and pipeline manipulation (`Select-Object`, `Sort-Object`, `Group-Object`, `Measure-Object`, `Compare-Object`, `New-Object`, `Add-Member`, `Get-Member`), formatting (`Format-List`, `Format-Table`, `Format-Wide`, `Format-Custom`, `Out-File`, `Out-String`), conversion and serialization (CSV, JSON, XML, CLIXML, HTML, Markdown), web commands (`Invoke-WebRequest`, `Invoke-RestMethod`), `Add-Type` (C# compilation through Roslyn), variables (`*-Variable`), tracing, events (`*-Event`, `Register-*Event`), debugging breakpoints, runspace commands, random numbers, mail, `Get-Date`, `Start-Sleep`, `Write-*` stream commands, `Out-GridView` and `Show-Command` (Windows UI) and others. Inventory in section 4 lists all of them.
Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Utility.security: Policy-relevant members: `Add-Type` (compiles and loads arbitrary code), `Invoke-Expression`, `Invoke-WebRequest`/`Invoke-RestMethod` (network egress, credentials), `Import-/Export-Clixml` and `ConvertFrom-CliXml` (deserialization), `New-Object` (type instantiation; constrained-language restrictions apply), `Unblock-File` (removes zone mark). `UNVERIFIED` until Phase 5 verifies each enforcement point.
Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Utility.performance: The `Select-Object`, `Sort-Object`, `Group-Object` family processes the whole pipeline in memory; no streaming guarantees are asserted here (`UNVERIFIED`).

lessons.text: Split the utility set by risk: pure data/formatting commands vs code-loading (`Add-Type`, `Invoke-Expression`) and network commands, so a policy can grant them independently.
Implement object-manipulation commands against the public cmdlet base-class API only, so third-party modules can replace them.

Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Utility.open: - `UNVERIFIED`: which Utility cmdlets are Windows-only beyond those with a visible `#if` condition (conditions are shown per row).

Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Management.purpose: Provider-facing and system-management commands: item/content/property commands over providers (`Get-ChildItem`, `Get-Item`, `Set-Content`, `New-Item`, `Copy-Item`, ... `*-ItemProperty`), location stack (`Get-Location`, `Set-Location`, `Push-Location`, `Pop-Location`), path commands (`Join-Path`, `Split-Path`, `Resolve-Path`, `Test-Path`, `Convert-Path`), drives and providers (`*-PSDrive`, `Get-PSProvider`), process and service commands, computer commands (`Restart-Computer`, `Stop-Computer`, `Rename-Computer`, `Get-ComputerInfo`, `Get-HotFix`), `Test-Connection`, time zone and clipboard commands. Platform-conditional classes carry an `#if` condition in section 4.
Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Management.security: The item/content commands are the user-facing entry to provider operations, so provider capability checks (`ShouldProcess`, credentials) apply (see [provider-model](../03-runtime/provider-model.md)). `Start-Process`, `Stop-Process`, service and computer commands act on the host OS.

lessons.text: Keep path- and item-commands provider-agnostic (the same verb set for files, registry, environment, functions) and let providers declare capabilities.
Route OS-level actions (process, service, computer) through an explicit capability so they can be denied per policy.

Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Management.open: - `UNVERIFIED`: evidence anchors above point to the start of the named files; Phase 5 will replace them with exact enforcement lines.

Microsoft.PowerShell.Security.purpose: Security commands and the certificate provider: execution policy (`Get-ExecutionPolicy`, `Set-ExecutionPolicy`), Authenticode (`Get-AuthenticodeSignature`, `Set-AuthenticodeSignature`), CMS encryption (`Protect-CmsMessage`, `Unprotect-CmsMessage`, `Get-CmsMessage`), file catalogs (`New-FileCatalog`, `Test-FileCatalog`), ACLs (`Get-Acl`, `Set-Acl`), credentials and secure strings (`Get-Credential`, `ConvertTo-SecureString`, `ConvertFrom-SecureString`), PFX certificates (`Get-PfxCertificate`), and one provider (the certificate store provider, `Microsoft.PowerShell.Security` project).
Microsoft.PowerShell.Security.security: This family is the user-facing side of the engine's security features; the enforcement itself lives in `src/System.Management.Automation/security/` (see Phase 5 `execution-policy.md`, `amsi-logging.md`). The assembly receives `InternalsVisibleTo` from the engine (see section 12 of `layered-architecture.md`).

lessons.text: Expose signature validation and policy queries as ordinary commands over a policy service so audit tooling can use the same API as users.
Do not rely on `SecureString` cmdlets as a secrets boundary; replace with an OS-keychain-backed secret type (see Phase 5 blueprint).

Microsoft.PowerShell.Security.open: - `UNVERIFIED`: file names in lesson evidence are anchors to the assembly's security sources; verify exact paths in Phase 5.

Microsoft.PowerShell.ConsoleHost.purpose: The console host assembly also defines the two transcript cmdlets, `Start-Transcript` and `Stop-Transcript`, because transcription is a host feature (`ConsoleHostTranscript.cs`, `StartTranscriptCmdlet.cs`, `StopTranscriptCmdlet.cs` under `host/msh`). The host itself is documented in [console-host](../04-hosting/console-host.md).

lessons.text: Keep transcription as a host service behind a command pair, so non-console hosts can supply their own sink.

Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Diagnostic.purpose: Windows diagnostics commands: `Get-Counter` (performance counters), `Get-WinEvent` and `New-WinEvent` (event log and ETW). Shipped only in Windows runtimes (the `powershell-win-core` project references it; `powershell-unix` does not).

lessons.text: Leave OS-specific diagnostics out of the initial command set and offer them as optional modules.

Microsoft.WSMan.Management.purpose: WS-Management client commands (`Connect-WSMan`, `Get-WSManInstance`, `Invoke-WSManAction`, `Set-WSManQuickConfig`, CredSSP commands, `Test-WSMan`) and the WSMan configuration provider. Windows-targeted; depends on `Microsoft.WSMan.Runtime` for session options.

lessons.text: Do not carry the WSMan command family into the new shell; remoting transport should be pluggable behind one session abstraction.

Microsoft.Management.Infrastructure.CimC.purpose: CIM/WMI commands built on `Microsoft.Management.Infrastructure` (`Get-CimInstance`, `New-CimSession`, `Invoke-CimMethod`, `Register-CimIndicationEvent`, ...). Shipped for Windows; grants `InternalsVisibleTo` to the DSC core configuration providers assembly.

lessons.text: Treat CIM/WMI as an optional adapter module, not part of the base command set.

Microsoft.WSMan.Runtime.purpose: Tiny shared runtime assembly with the WSMan session-option types (`SessionOption`, `ProxyAccessType`, `ProxyAuthentication`) used by `Microsoft.WSMan.Management`; contains no cmdlets.

Microsoft.PowerShell.GraphicalHost.purpose: WPF-based UI assembly (project `Microsoft.Management.UI.Internal`, assembly `Microsoft.PowerShell.GraphicalHost`) behind `Out-GridView`, `Show-Command` and `Get-Help -ShowWindow`; included only when the build uses the WindowsDesktop SDK (conditional `ProjectReference` in `powershell-win-core.csproj`). The engine reaches it through a reflection wrapper (`src/System.Management.Automation/utils/GraphicalHostReflectionWrapper.cs`). Contains no cmdlets.

lessons.text: Keep GUI helpers behind a late-bound host service (reflection or plug-in) so the engine never references UI assemblies.

Microsoft.PowerShell.CoreCLR.Eventing.purpose: Small Windows-only assembly (`EventProvider`, `EventDescriptor`, `EventProviderTraceListener`, native wrappers) giving .NET Core code access to ETW; referenced by `System.Management.Automation` only when `IsWindows` is true and granted `InternalsVisibleTo` back to the engine. Contains no cmdlets.

lessons.text: Use the platform's standard structured-logging/ETW abstractions (`EventSource`, OpenTelemetry) instead of a private ETW wrapper.
